title: The Prismatic System
description: The Prismatic System is a compact formal symbolic language built from four layers — elements, binding, folding, and chains. Each layer introduces new rules that depend on everything before it, making it an excellent test of logical reasoning and step-by-step problem solving.
studyNote: This course was used in the original Coast learning study. Work through the four layers in order; each section maps directly to one lecture.

highlights.label: Layer 1 · Elements
highlights.desc: Three element types and the value rules that govern them

highlights.label: Layer 2 · Binding
highlights.desc: The binding operation (⊕) and its six type-and-order rules

highlights.label: Layer 3 · Folding
highlights.desc: The folding operation (∆) and conditional transformation rules

highlights.label: Layer 4 · Chains
highlights.desc: Multi-step sequences that combine every rule you've learned

title: The Science of Cooking
description: A four-lecture deep dive into the chemistry and physics behind everyday cooking — from the Maillard reaction and emulsification to gluten networks and the thermodynamics of bread rising. Inspired by Harvard's Science and Cooking curriculum.
studyNote: Work through the four lectures in order. Each section covers one lecture and its interactive kitchen diagnostics.

highlights.label: Lecture 1 · Maillard Reaction
highlights.desc: Non-enzymatic browning, flavor synthesis, and thermal kinetics

highlights.label: Lecture 2 · Emulsification
highlights.desc: Surfactants, interfacial tension, and stable emulsions

highlights.label: Lecture 3 · Gluten Network
highlights.desc: Gliadin, glutenin, and the viscoelastic dough matrix

highlights.label: Lecture 4 · Leavening
highlights.desc: Fermentation, gas laws, and why bread rises
